metrics.method: Full history 2026-05-28 to 2026-08-04, 308 non-service messages (167 client, 141 ours) plus 10 service events. client_questions_total = client messages containing '?'. unanswered_over_24h is a MANUAL read for a substantive answer, not a next-message check: the automated 'next team message >24h' test returns only 1, because someone almost always replied quickly with an acknowledgement. max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive non-client messages. Promises = explicit will/we'll/let-me commitments by our side, scored kept/lapsed against later chat evidence.

churn_timeline.event: Onboarded. Eric opens the group, five staff introduce themselves over the next four days. She submits the intake form the same afternoon.

We find the previous team still logged into her OnlyFans. Mayson tells her to change the password; she posts the new credentials straight into the group chat. Nobody flags it, nothing is rotated, and the credentials sit in the history to this day.
Her booked kickoff call with Mica silently fails - no calendar invite reached either side. She chases her own booking and the call is improvised the same afternoon.
Day 3: subscribers collapse from an average of 60-70/day to 4. Fred explains it honestly and promises a push. This is the last performance number she is ever given.
She reports that all of her socials appear shadowbanned. No diagnosis, no escalation; she works around it herself by switching to her personal TikTok.
She posts her Instagram login and then a live 2FA code in the chat so we can link a Facebook page we create in ALTR's own estate, with no login for her.
She asks about the paid promo Derrek sold her. Answered with a hand-off tag to someone not in the conversation. Never started, never mentioned again.
First invoice cannot be paid: no phone on the Zelle, then no email, then the wrong email. She sends ~20 leak links to the DMCA topic on the same day.
She asks for the Miami/Orlando shoot Derrek pitched. On 6/8 Mica says photographers have been contacted and is 'following up now'. Never raised again by anyone.
Invoice #1 abandoned after nine days of failed payment attempts on our rails and rolled into the next one.
She discovers that the 13 voice notes she recorded for the chatters were never processed. Fred redoes them and thanks her for pointing it out.
Invoice #2 arrives on a third payment rail (a Mercury link). She disputes commission on $200 + ~$383 of self-run live earnings.
'let me work with the team to get this resolved and get back to you.' Six days of silence follow.
Fourth rail (Chase). On 6/23 we tell her the Mercury link was incorrect, restate the total as $931.81, and she pays the same evening.
Weekly takedown graphic: 197 infringements removed.
'Hi all those leaks are still up.' She re-sends ten fresh links in the following eight minutes. Answered with 'I sent the team the links... they will be taken down'.
Identical complaint, second time in 48 hours: 'All those leaks are still up were you able to report them'. Nothing escalates. 6/29: 'let me check on this with the team'.
Fifth banking change in 33 days (Bank of America, 'last change I promise!'), plus a generic two-stage DMCA process explanation instead of per-link status.
She stops asking and starts setting terms: calculates the invoice herself, deducts her own live earnings, sends $981.
Still doing our DMCA intake work for us - sends two more leak links, one day before quitting.
Sends the wire, then resigns 21 minutes later: 'I'm going to take over my account and work independently'. Volunteers a final balance and photographs the figure.
No reply. Not that day, not that week, not in the 53 days since - from anyone, including the owner.
Mica sends routine reel inspo and Michelle sends the weekly leak report, four days after the resignation. The templates had not noticed.
23 consecutive days of zero messages from ALTR follow.
First post-churn human contact, 27 days late, and it is a request for her earning statements so we can bill her.
'Just making sure you saw this.' The last message ALTR has ever sent this client. No exit conversation, no win-back attempt, no offboarding, no access revocation.
53 days silent. Final invoice for 7/1-7/7 still unissued, 44 days past our own cadence date; the exit balance she volunteered has never been chased or even written down.

warning_signs_missed: 2026-05-30 - Subscribers fell from 60-70/day to 4 on day 3. We explained it once and then never reported another growth or revenue number for the remaining 37 days. A client who stops receiving numbers stops being able to justify the fee.

2026-05-31 - 'I think like all my socials are shadow banned' was treated as a conversational aside rather than a platform incident. She then spent five weeks producing content into damaged accounts and self-diagnosing.

2026-06-02 - A question about promo Derrek sold her in the pitch was closed with an @-tag to someone not in the conversation. An unfulfilled pre-sale promise with no owner is the classic churn seed, and nothing in our process reopens it.
2026-06-11 - The client caught our failure, not us: 13 voice notes had silently failed to upload. When the client is doing our QA, our internal checks have already failed.

2026-06-15 - A commission dispute is a repricing conversation. She flagged that she wanted her own live earnings excluded; we never wrote a policy, so on 7/2 she simply started deducting it herself. A client who has begun setting her own terms has already half-left.

2026-06-26 and 2026-06-28 - The same complaint twice in 48 hours, both times answered with a status graphic or a process explanation instead of a per-link result. Repeat of an identical complaint is the most reliable churn predictor in this dataset and no rule escalates it.
2026-07-01 - Our third bank change in 30 days landed in the same week as her loudest unresolved complaint. Nobody was looking at the account as a whole, so nobody saw the friction compounding.
2026-07-05 - She was still doing our DMCA intake for us the day before she quit. Her remaining effort was all going into the one thing we had not fixed - that is what an exhausted client looks like.

2026-07-10 - Two templated broadcasts fired four days after she resigned. The signal we missed here is about ourselves: our outbound is on autopilot and nobody reads these chats, which is why a resignation could sit unanswered for 53 days.
top_fix: Give every account one named owner whose job is closing complaints with evidence rather than routing them. Hannah's two loudest issues - leaks still live, and the paid promo she was sold - were each answered with a status graphic or an @-tag and then dropped, and both were still open the day she left. The same owner would have had to reply to her resignation within 24 hours instead of letting two templated broadcasts and a collections chase be the last things she heard from us.
